ui.habitat_title: Habitat — real NASA ISS cabin data (context only, not scored)
ui.habitat_intro: Real telemetry from the NASA OSDR Environmental Data App, mission RR-1 (2014). CO2 is shown as an hourly mean in mmHg (ppm converted at 760 mmHg total pressure) against the NASA-STD-3001 habitat requirement (average one-hour CO2 partial pressure of 3 mmHg or less). The converted values are an approximation, not a compliance statement.
ui.habitat_flag: Flagged ARTIFACT: CO2 stayed at exactly {ppm:,.0f} ppm ({mm:.1f} mmHg) for {hours:.0f} h in the raw 5-minute series. Origin unknown (sensor or data fill). It is never shown as normal.

ui.habitat_table_note: {n} missions. A constant run of at least 1 h exists in {k} of them. Zero or capped sensor values are marked. Rodent-research facility sensors, location and calibration not documented: do not read these rows as crew exposure.
ui.habitat_credit: Data and visualizations are courtesy of the Environmental Data App (EDA), https://visualization.osdr.nasa.gov/eda/. Requirement: NASA OCHMO-TB-004 Rev B (NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 2 Rev C, V2 6004).

ui.trend_title: Indicators over time — each against this astronaut's own baseline
ui.trend_intro: The line is the daily value, the flat line is the personal baseline (days 1 to 5), and the third line is the point where the rule starts counting a day as unfavourable (1.5 standard deviations on the unfavourable side). A day is flagged when two days in a row cross it. These are design parameters, not clinical limits. Synthetic crew.

ui.trend_building: Days 1 to 5 build the personal baseline: no drift is evaluated yet.

ui.hazard_intro: Hazard names are those of the NASA Human Research Program. A hazard that C-Sync does not measure is shown as such, never as fine.

hazard_rows.watched: Reported sleep, sleepiness, stress, mood and workload against the personal baseline (Morale).
Works offline; reports wait in a send queue and arrive once; resume is refused on stale data. Ground delay in the demo: 20 min (NASA: up to 22 min one way).
Resting heart rate against the personal baseline; blood pressure in the guided procedure. Bone density and immune changes are not measured.

ui.hazard_source: Source: NASA Human Research Program, 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight, https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/hazards/ ; delay: NASA ASCEND 2022, NTRS 20220013418.
ui.cm_title: What NASA already documents as countermeasures — reference, not a prescription
ui.cm_intro: C-Sync does not choose, dose or schedule any countermeasure. It points to the onboard procedure and leaves the decision to the crew medical officer and the flight surgeon. The rows below are what NASA publishes, with the source.

cm_rows.nasa: On the International Space Station, exercise with a treadmill, a cycle ergometer and a resistive device is used to protect muscle strength, aerobic fitness, bone density and sensorimotor performance. NASA is now testing whether a treadmill is still needed (study in progress, no results yet).
cm_rows.csync: Does not measure exercise. No recommendation.

cm_rows.nasa: NASA lists sleep loss, circadian desynchronization and work overload as a risk. An in-flight lighting schedule exists on the Station for circadian adaptation. NASA states that validated, individualised countermeasures are still a research gap.
cm_rows.csync: Reported sleep (PH09) below the personal baseline for 2 days opens procedure PROC-FATIGUE-01 and refers to the crew medical officer.
cm_rows.source: NASA Human Research Roadmap, risk 100; gap Sleep-102; task 1453
